knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 - \frac{2}{x} - \frac{2}{x^{2}}$. Rewrite with powers, then differentiate term by term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(-2x^{-1})+(-2x^{-2})+(2)\\
f'(x)&=\frac{2}{x^{2}} + \frac{4}{x^{3}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=\frac{2}{\left(2\right)^{2}} + \frac{4}{\left(2\right)^{3}}=1
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(1\right)}=-1.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)&=-1\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- x+\left(2\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
y&=\frac{5}{2} - x
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=-1$ and $b=\frac{5}{2}$.
